definitions.explanation: a traditional Japanese celebration held on the seventh night after a baby's birth, when the baby's name is formally announced

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんのお{七夜|しちや}を{祝|いわ}った。
examples.english: We celebrated the baby's seventh-night ceremony.

examples.japanese: お{七夜|しちや}に{命名書|めいめいしょ}を{書|か}いて{飾|かざ}る。
examples.english: On the seventh night, they write out and display the naming certificate.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}はお{七夜|しちや}を{簡単|かんたん}に{済|す}ませる{家庭|かてい}も{多|おお}いが、{命名|めいめい}のお{祝|いわ}いだけは{大切|たいせつ}にしたい。
examples.english: These days many families keep the seventh-night celebration simple, but they still want to make the naming ceremony special.

notes:
A traditional Japanese ceremony held on the seventh night after a baby's birth. The main purpose is the formal naming of the child. The baby's name is written on a {命名書|めいめいしょ} (naming certificate) and displayed in the home.

CEREMONY CUSTOMS:
- {命名書|めいめいしょ} — a calligraphied card or paper announcing the baby's name, displayed on the wall or at the family altar
- {祝|いわ}い{膳|ぜん} — a celebratory meal, traditionally including {尾頭付|おかしらつ}きの{鯛|たい} (whole sea bream) and {赤飯|せきはん} (red bean rice)
- Family members and close relatives gather to meet the baby

RELATED CELEBRATIONS:
- {宮参|みやまい}り / お{宮参|みやまい}り — first shrine visit (around 30 days after birth)
- {百日祝|ももかいわ}い / お{食|く}い{初|ぞ}め — 100-day celebration with symbolic first meal
- {初節句|はつぜっく} — first seasonal festival after birth

USAGE:
Also written without the honorific お as {七夜|しちや}, but the お{七夜|しちや} form is far more common.
